causal.assumptions_right: The United States coupon curve stayed high, the SOFR strip still prices above the 3.88 fixing, and the dollar did not collapse versus other majors. Direction versus Canada was right enough to produce a large peak and leave the book still green versus entry.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Three-digit crude and a rising Canadian relative impulse were treated as secondary overlays on a rates short of Canada. They are first-order for the Canadian leg. Harvest discipline on a material winner was underweighted versus letting the original dollar story run after the peak.
causal.causal_divergence: The peak-to-now giveback is a Canadian-leg squeeze from oil and a better Canadian impulse, not a bust of the United States rate story. Holding full size after that mix showed up converted a paid winner into a large giveback without a new dollar-negative catalyst.
causal.future_implication: Dollar-Canada size has to be conditioned on oil and the Canadian impulse. A still-valid United States rate view is not a license to hold full size in a commodity currency after a material win has already paid.
causal.observed_reality: The pair did pay to a large peak, then gave most of that open profit back as oil held in three digits and Canada's relative impulse turned higher while United States two-year and ten-year yields remained 4.79 and 5.12.
causal.original_belief: United States rate and growth premium versus a soft Canada would keep dollar-Canada trending higher, with restrictive United States policy dominating oil and local Canadian data, so the long could be held through noise after a good entry near 1.401.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same three-digit oil and the same rising Canadian factor visible into the peak, a harvest cut into strength would have locked most of the peak and left a runner. Same information, smaller size after those Canadian positives printed, would have avoided the bulk of the giveback.

items.what_happened_vs_expected: The expected path was a grind higher in dollar-Canada while United States yields stayed restrictive versus Canada. The realized path was an overshoot to a large peak, then a giveback as oil held above 100 and Canada's relative impulse improved. Residual profit is still positive versus entry but far below the maximum favorable excursion, which is a harvest failure rather than a thesis reversal on the dollar leg.

causal.assumptions_right: The United States cash and coupon premium versus Canada remained the correct dollar-versus-Canada side, and the first harvest cut itself was the right reaction to three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Fifteen million was treated as already-underwritten residual size. At 1.40458 after an 80 percent open-profit giveback, that leftover was winner size, not the size a flat book would start.
causal.causal_divergence: The giveback is leftover-size path against still-rising Canadian impulse and still-high Brent, not a collapse of the United States rate leg. WTI leaving three digits arrived as a CAD-negative oil shift but did not offset the leftover winner size.
causal.future_implication: After a material USDCAD harvest, remaining United States rate edge must be re-sized from the current print as if flat. Still-green versus entry is not permission to keep the leftover winner ticket.
causal.observed_reality: Expected the US-CA rate gap to keep a USD/CAD long valid and expected three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse to force harvest rather than peak-size hold. That harvest ran (20m to 15m). Giveback of about 80 percent of MFE on the residual was larger than a clean hold-the-reduced-book path; WTI at 97.15 is friendlier to remaining USD/CAD edge than the prior three-digit oil regime, but it did not arrive as a full offset to rising prima and CAD hike pricing. Peak open profit was not a level the 15m book was entitled to keep.
causal.original_belief: Material USDCAD winner already harvested once last cycle, 20m cut to 15m, under a still-valid US-over-Canada rate gap.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same giveback, the same rising Canadian impulse, and the same 1.40458 print visible, a further cut to a size a flat book would initiate would have avoided carrying winner size through ordinary adverse variance.

items.no_new_lesson: No new lesson: further giveback after the first harvest cut is ordinary variance around a still-green residual. The prior process remains sound — oil plus a rising Canadian impulse is a harvest trigger, and leftover United States rate edge belongs in reduced size rather than winner size.
items.what_happened_vs_expected: Expected the US-CA rate gap to keep a USD/CAD long valid and expected three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse to force harvest rather than peak-size hold. That harvest ran (20m to 15m). Giveback of about 80 percent of MFE on the residual was larger than a clean hold-the-reduced-book path; WTI at 97.15 is friendlier to remaining USD/CAD edge than the prior three-digit oil regime, but it did not arrive as a full offset to rising prima and CAD hike pricing. Peak open profit was not a level the 15m book was entitled to keep.

causal.assumptions_right: The dollar still has a clean rate advantage versus CAD, USDCAD is the right dollar-spot expression of that gap, and a leftover rates stub can remain after harvest.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse is a harvest catalyst at winner size, not residual noise; the hike poll compresses policy optics on the CAD leg.
causal.causal_divergence: The rate-gap thesis still explains why some dollar-versus-CAD edge exists. It does not explain keeping winner size after the harvest trigger printed. The break is post-extension sizing, not a failed dollar-versus-CAD expression.
causal.future_implication: After a material USDCAD win, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse remains the harvest trigger; leftover US rate edge is expressed in reduced size, not winner size.
causal.observed_reality: A material winner then a large giveback, with spot through entry, coincident with three-digit oil, rising Canadian impulse, and a Bank of Canada hike poll to 2.50.
causal.original_belief: The US-Canada rate gap would keep winner-size long USDCAD intact through oil and CAD-impulse noise after the material extension.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: The same frozen tape already implied cutting winner size and, at most, a reduced residual long. Holding 8 million was not implied by the rate gap alone; initiating 8 million from flat on this packet would also have been a no.

items.no_new_lesson: This is ordinary variance around the prior harvest rule: after a material USDCAD win, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse is the known harvest trigger. The original process remains sound if winner size is now cut and only a residual rate stub is kept.
items.what_happened_vs_expected: The book treated the SOFR/CORRA and US2/CA2 gap as sufficient to hold winner-size long USDCAD after a material run. Observed path was a large giveback with spot now 1.3995 through the 1.401 entry, while three-digit oil, rising Canadian impulse, and a Bank of Canada hike poll supported CAD. That is harvest-trigger tape, not a dip that validates winner size.
